title: Descent of homogeneous cocycles through cohomology
statement: Given an equivalence between homogeneous degree-two cocycles and explicit inhomogeneous two-cocycles compatible with degree-one boundaries, the homogeneous cohomology is equivalent to the quotient by continuous coboundaries.

proof.text: Construct explicit LeftHomologyData on the short complex in degrees (1,2,3), using TopModuleCat.isLimitKer and TopModuleCat.isColimitCoker. Its homologyIso, composed with HomologicalComplex.homologyIsoSc' 1 2 3, identifies continuous H2 with the algebraic quotient of the degree-two differential kernel by the range of the degree-one differential lifted to that kernel.

For invariant degree-one cochains evaluate at (1,g); reconstruct a continuous one-cochain b as rho(a)(b(a⁻¹c)), currying once. The recursive degree-one differential evaluated at (1,g,gh) is rho(g)(b(h)) - b(gh) + b(g). Both this formula and the reconstruction evaluation identity are proved explicitly.

Show that the submodule quotient relation x-y in the boundary range is exactly the continuous coboundary relation on the canonical degree-two coordinates. Negate the range membership to use y-x. In the forward direction evaluate the lifted boundary equation and use the degree-one formula. In the reverse direction reconstruct the homogeneous one-cochain from b; injectivity of degree-two coordinates proves its lifted differential equals y-x.

Apply Quotient.congr to the canonical kernel-to-inhomogeneous-cocycle equivalence and the proved equivalence of relations. Compose with the concrete homology equivalence. The supplied abstract cocycle equivalence is not needed for compatibility: the proof constructs the canonical one and proves its boundary compatibility directly.
